title: Residency policy DSL, pin priority, and exportable audit bundles for Hosted API
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Problem statement: Customers need a concise, machine-readable way to express residency constraints for Hosted API traffic, control priority when multiple pins or affinity rules apply, and generate tamper-evident evidence bundles for audits. Current controls are fragmented across routing rules, tenancy metadata, and manual evidence exports.

Scope: Design and deliver a policy DSL (text-first, JSON/YAML serializable) that operators can use to express residency and retention requirements, implement pin-priority semantics in the request router so multiple matching policies are resolved deterministically, add a server-side 'audit bundle' export that collects routing decisions, retention metadata, and signed evidence artifacts for a given tenant/time-range, and provide an editor in Console to author policies and preview routing outcomes.

Out of scope: Private/VPC packaging and air-gapped export paths (handled by Private team), long-term archival storage for evidence bundles (we will provide export and signed package, storage is customer-managed), transformation of existing tenant configs (we will provide migration tooling and a compatibility shim).

Goals:
- Create an expressive but audit-friendly policy DSL that supports geo-anchoring, hard/soft pin modes, retention constraints, allowed-region lists, and temporal windows.
- Add deterministic conflict resolution via pin priority integer and explicit fallback chains.
- Implement an API to request signed audit bundles that include routing decisions, model variant used, retention TTLs, and evidence of delete/retention policy application.
- Expose a Console policy editor with syntax validation, preview simulator, and one-click export of audit bundles.

Success metrics:
- Policy DSL covers 95% of enterprise residency requests (measured from 50 recent customer cases).
- Routing determinism tests pass at 100% across 5000 synthetic policy permutations.
- Audit bundle generation latency < 30s for 24h tenant window on standard infra.

Notes on backward compatibility: We will implement a compatibility layer that maps existing region pins to the DSL with a default priority. Customers will be prompted via Console to review and publish the converted policy.
acceptance_criteria: DSL grammar and schema published in Confluence and validated with sample customer rules
Router implements priority integer and fallback chain semantics; unit + integration tests demonstrate deterministic resolution
Console editor supports create/edit/validate/preview and shows routing trace for sample requests
Audit bundle API returns a signed .tar.gz containing routing traces, retention metadata, and an evidence manifest. Bundle verified by a signature verification step in QA
Migration tool converts existing tenant pins to DSL with a dry-run report and customer-visible diff
Security review completed and threat-model mitigations documented
technical_notes: Policy DSL should be a minimal superset of existing rule attributes: region_tags, region_list[], pin_mode (hard|soft|prefer), priority:int, retention_ttl_seconds:int, start/end timestamps
Router change: evaluate candidate policies, sort by priority desc, apply first matching hard pin; for soft pins allow fallback but increment metrics for SLA reports
Store published policy as immutable versions; include policy version id in request trace and audit bundle
Audit bundle contents: policy-version.json, request-trace.log (per-request routing decisions), model_variant.txt, retention-actions.log, signatures/*.sig
Bundle signing: use platform KMS to sign manifest; include KMS key id in manifest for verifiability
Retention enforcement hook: async worker that reconciles objects older than TTL and logs delete/retain decisions for bundle generation
Performance: add caching layer for policy evaluation keyed by (tenant, api-route, sequence-length-bucket) to keep per-request latency impact < 3ms
RBAC: only org-admins + compliance-roles can publish policies; viewer roles can preview and request audit bundles
